reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape for a compliant finding; the rendered p0001 is byte-identical to the original, so no invalid or directionally wrong edit exists.

The cited text supports compliance: Section 1 imposes only a service-enablement duty to provide 'reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services' — not a right to audit, inspect or verify Customer books, usage or systems. Absence of any Vendor audit right is more favourable to us than the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access), so there is nothing to limit.

The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is explained by the total absence of an audit clause rather than by unlimited audit rights; it is not evidence of a walk-away term here. Treating this as 'missing' would be wrong because the rule exists to cap a Vendor right adverse to us, not to procure one.

Rationale is accurate and appropriately notes the residual risk (audit/system-access language could be introduced via an Exhibit or amendment), which is the right internal-evidence treatment rather than a negotiation issue.
